fields.v: Workflow matters: SDAgent-DT best mean ImplRate 49.48% (Pro 53.50%), Single 45.72%, DDT lowest 27.71%; authors attribute DDT's drop to errors in the design document propagating downstream, and Single's to interleaved code-test loops (first test at step 11.56 vs 27.96 for DT). Flash matched or beat Pro on ImplRate (Single: 48.46% vs 42.97%) at about four times the tokens sent. Cost per project $4.85-$7.05. Across three runs DT jointly fulfilled 796 requirements, 526 by one run only. No leakage drop on 2025-Q1 projects (42% vs 40%). Failures: missing features 32.4%, incorrect implementation 34.1%; root causes task planning 55.8%, execution 38.6%, verification 5.7%. No significance tests

fields.v: Distinguished workflows (27.71% to 49.48% mean ImplRate); judge agreement with humans comparable to inter-human agreement (pairwise 76.7-84.4% vs 78.4-88.1%; Pearson 0.62-0.67); three runs showed a large common core but many run-specific successes. Limitations stated: possible implementation errors in the unified framework; only two Gemini models; reliance on LLM judge (validated on 10 projects)

fields.v: Limitations: possible implementation errors in the authors' framework; only Gemini-2.5-Pro and Flash; benchmark quality depends on human-revised requirements; LLM-judge reliability. Gaps: agents fulfil only about half of requirements; main bottleneck is planning and requirement comprehension (omission, misinterpretation) and weak self-verification; premature self-submission by stronger models; cost-effective best-of-N aggregation; better agent orchestration and task decomposition
